name: Cervical Aortic Arch

criteria.description: Aortic arch located abnormally high in the cervical region above the clavicle
Presence of vascular ring causing tracheoesophageal compression
Confirmation of cervical aortic arch by CT angiography or MRI
Symptoms related to vascular compression such as stridor or dysphagia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging confirmation of aortic arch located in cervical region with or without clinical symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on imaging studies; no standardized formal diagnostic criteria exist.

pathognomonic.notes: Visible or palpable pulsation in the neck due to high aortic arch
Leads to stridor and respiratory distress

searchTerms: swallowing problems due to esophageal compression

common.notes: High-pitched inspiratory sound from airway obstruction
Due to airway compression and impaired clearance
Soft tissue swelling over the cervical aortic arch

occasional.notes: Due to recurrent laryngeal nerve irritation
Non-specific discomfort related to vascular anomaly
Transient loss of consciousness possibly due to vascular compromise
Ischemic symptoms due to altered blood flow

searchTerms: high blood pressure in lung arteries
increased pressure in lungs' blood vessels

rare.notes: Rare complication of abnormal aortic arch anatomy
Very rare, due to altered cerebral blood flow
searchTerms: brain symptoms from low blood flow
neurological problems due to poor brain perfusion
deficits caused by reduced cerebral blood flow

imaging: CT angiography showing aortic arch positioned at cervical level
MRI angiography confirming aberrant arch anatomy
Echocardiography may show associated cardiac anomalies
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; sporadic cases reported
other: Physical exam revealing pulsatile neck mass

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of two aortic arches forming a complete vascular ring
Typically diagnosed in infancy with severe respiratory symptoms
Aortic arch located on the right side of the trachea
May or may not cause vascular ring symptoms

redFlags: Signs of vascular compromise such as syncope or upper limb ischemia
references: Backer CL, Mavroudis C. Cervical aortic arch: surgical management and outcomes. Ann Thorac Surg. 2010;89(3):1027-1032.
Mohan JC, et al. Cervical aortic arch: clinical and imaging features. Cardiovasc Intervent Radiol. 2015;38(1):117-124.
